rationale.edition: All 16 changed files live in OSS-owned paths: web/src/** (Vue components, composable, service, i18n, icon registry) and src/api/management/src/** (alert request/response models and the list handler). No enterprise-owned directory appears in changed_files.txt, and the #[cfg(feature = "enterprise")] annotation in request/alerts/mod.rs is a compile-time feature gate, not enterprise code ownership. No enterprise keywords (cipher/SSO/SAML/RBAC/SDR/sensitive-data/logo-management) are present, so edition is oss.
rationale.skip: Not skipped. trigger_comment.txt is empty (no skip request or tests-added marker) and feature_hint.txt is empty. The change is user-facing: it adds a 'Used by' column and an impact dialog to the alerts UI, so the no-user-facing-change skip does not apply.
rationale.e2e: E2E is warranted. The diff introduces new user-exercisable UI flows: a 'Used by' column on the alert destination and template lists, a click-to-open DependencyImpactDialog (with search, lane highlights, open-in-new-tab, and confirmed delete), and cache invalidation that refreshes those columns after mutations. These are brand-new interactive flows in web/src that a browser test should exercise.
rationale.area: Alerts. The bulk of the changes live under web/src/components/alerts/ and web/src/composables/alerts/, backed by the alert list API under src/api/management/src. Sibling Playwright specs already exist under tests/ui-testing/playwright-tests/Alerts/, so this area is the natural home.
rationale.group: Alerts. The OSS ci-matrix base manifest defines an 'Alerts' testfolder shard (actual_folder 'Alerts') that runs alerts-*.spec.js files such as alerts-ui-operations.spec.js and alerts-destinations-prebuilt.spec.js, which is the closest existing matrix group for this feature.
rationale.existing_tests: No E2E specs in the diff. The only changed test files are Vitest unit specs (DependencyImpactDialog.spec.ts, DependencyUsageCell.spec.ts, useDependencyGraph.spec.ts) under web/src/** — these are unit tests, not Playwright E2E coverage, and do not cover the new feature at the browser level.
